newsitem.title: SWEDEN: MoDo sees NorScan stocks up without slower output.
newsitem.headline: MoDo sees NorScan stocks up without slower output.

text.p: Pulp stocks held by North American and Scandinavian (NorScan) producers risk rising by the year end if the pace of production is not cut in the second half of 1997, Sweden's MoDo Paper said on Tuesday.
"The risk that stocks will increase in the summer and autumn must unfortunately be seen as rather large," Modo Papers market analyst Soren Nordin wrote in a company's newsletter.
He said if the rate of production was not reduced in the second half of the year, NorScan stocks could rise to about 1.9 million tonnes by the end of the year -- the same level as at the end of 1996.
Stocks are currently around 1.6 million tonnes which is equivalent to about 27 days of delivery.
Nordin said this increase in stocks would be due to an imbalance between the capacity usage by NorScan producers and deliveries.

Capacity usage rose to about 90 percent among NorScan producers in the first five months of 1997. It was estimated that for the full year NorScan deliveries would rise to about 90 percent of capacity.
